Participants will evaluate emerging startups, assess market opportunities, analyse business models and financial performance, and identify the ventures with the strongest potential for scalable growth and long-term returns. Through a case-based format inspired by real-world venture capital decision-making, teams will develop an investment thesis, conduct due diligence, evaluate valuations and risks, and recommend an investment strategy backed by data and strategic reasoning. The challenge goes beyond identifying promising businesses: participants must justify where to invest, why to invest, how much to invest, and what it would take to generate meaningful returns. XPitch aims to test analytical rigour, commercial judgment, financial acumen, and the ability to make compelling, evidence-backed investment decisions under uncertainty. The objective is simple: think like a venture capitalist, evaluate like an investor, and build a case for the next big bet.

additions.description: About the Hackathon Speed Demon is a 72-hour online performance championship built around one challenge: make your code faster, leaner, and more efficient. Most hackathons ask a panel whether they liked your idea. Speed Demon measures whether your code actually performs. Every track provides a task specification, a dataset, and a deliberately naive reference implementation that solves the problem correctly and slowly. Your challenge is to solve the same problem correctly — and not slowly. The competition covers five tracks: log processing, search indexing, complex CSV parsing and joining, graph algorithms, and lossless compression. Each track tests a different aspect of performance engineering, from memory layout and parsing efficiency to shortest-path algorithms and compression trade-offs. This is not a hackathon where you submit benchmark numbers from your own laptop. We run your code ourselves. Every submission is built from your Dockerfile and executed on the same dedicated machine in Helsinki, with fixed CPU resources, memory limits, and a controlled benchmarking environment. The implementation must: Read input from the designated /data directory. We evaluate whether the final implementation works, whether the optimization decisions are technically sound, and whether the team can explain and defend the software it built. The submission must respect the official CPU, memory, timeout, and sandbox restrictions. The GitHub repository must be public at code freeze.
